fact_sheet.business_description: The Company supplies routers and switches that carry Internet traffic and corporate data [D01]. It operates as an equipment provider for expanding network capacity, positioning itself as an infrastructure franchise within the technology sector [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Routers and switches sold to enterprise, service-provider, and smaller-business customers [D01].
Customers benefit from installed networks, trained administrators, and compatibility advantages, which may encourage repeat purchases and product standardization [D01].
economics: Revenue grew 53% in the fiscal second quarter; GAAP net income was $825 million compared to $282 million in the prior year [D01, D02].
Pro-forma net income of $906 million excludes items such as purchased in-process R&D, acquisition costs, and goodwill amortization [D02, D03].
Capital intensity includes recurring R&D and acquisitions to fill product gaps, though specific maintenance capex figures are not in pack [D01, D02, D06].
earnings_record: Fiscal second-quarter GAAP EPS was $0.23 (versus $0.08 prior year) and six-month GAAP EPS was $0.34 [D01].
Pro-forma quarterly EPS was $0.25 (versus $0.17 prior year) and six-month pro-forma EPS was $0.48 [D01].
competitive_position: Competitors include Lucent, Nortel, and Juniper [D06].
The company possesses advantages in product breadth and customer familiarity, though it faces risks from technological substitution and rapid product cycles [D01, D05, D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Seven completed acquisitions discussed; three accounted for as poolings [D01].
No specific debt, cash balance, or leverage figures provided in the pack [D02].
management_and_capital_allocation: Management reports increasing adoption of products by businesses and governments [D01].
Strategy focuses on acquisitions to fill product gaps [D01].
price_and_valuation: No contemporaneous March 1 stock price or P/E ratio available in pack [D02, D04].
Mechanically, $0.23 quarterly GAAP EPS annualizes to $0.92; $0.25 pro-forma EPS annualizes to $1.00 [D02, D05].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Rapid equipment changes requiring constant engineering or acquisitions [D05].
Possibility of competitive displacement or a slowdown in capital spending [D05].
Complexities in per-share earnings due to pooling restatements, acquired R&D, and share issuance [D05].
recent_events: February 8, 2000: Results and two-for-one stock split announced [D07].
berkshire_context: Existing portfolio includes consumer and financial franchises like Coca-Cola, American Express, and Gillette [D08].
Berkshire emphasizes identifying if a new security fits within incremental allocation needs for a permanent-capital enterprise [D08].
missing_data: Contemporaneous March 1 stock price, full balance sheet (cash/debt), maintenance capex figures, and normalized owner-earnings calculations.

final.memo:
We have reviewed the business, which acts as a supplier of routers and switches for network infrastructure [D01]. While the company has shown rapid revenue growth in the short term, our primary requirement is a business that we can understand and evaluate over the long term [D01, D08].

Unlike the wonderful businesses we prefer—which possess durable moats and pricing power—this company operates in an environment of rapid technological change [D01, D05]. Success here requires constant, heavy R&D spending and a steady stream of acquisitions just to avoid being rendered obsolete by competitors such as Lucent, Nortel, or Juniper [D01, D05, D06].

We find it difficult to ascertain an owner-minded management style when growth is driven by frequent acquisitions and complex accounting practices, such as pooling [D01, D05]. Furthermore, the lack of transparent balance sheet data prevents us from assessing the true capital structure or the level of debt, both of which are critical to our evaluation of risk [D02].

Given the uncertainty surrounding the company's long-term economics and the high risk of permanent capital loss from technological displacement, we have no basis to value the enterprise [D01, D05]. We prefer to keep our capital in stable, predictable franchises and will continue to wait for an opportunity that fits our criteria [D08].
